questions.q: What does the FeedbackScope capstone project do, per this lesson?
options: Takes customer feedback text and returns a sentiment score and label
Trains a new sentiment model from scratch on user data
Manages Kubernetes clusters across multiple regions
Generates Dockerfiles automatically from source code
questions.explain: FeedbackScope is a FastAPI service with one endpoint that returns a sentiment score and label for a piece of feedback text.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the capstone was deliberately scoped to one model and one endpoint?
options: Because more complex models are technically impossible to containerize
Because the course only allows one endpoint per service
Because autoscaling only works with single-endpoint services
Because the point is proving you can take something real through the entire deployment pipeline, not build the most elaborate app
questions.explain: A small, finished, fully-deployed project beats a bigger, half-built one -- that's the stated reasoning for keeping scope small.

questions.q: According to this lesson's structure, what gets built in Lesson 24?
options: The initial Dockerfile and first deploy
A real autoscaling policy, a health check endpoint, and a caching decision
The final portfolio presentation
A completely new, unrelated project
questions.explain: Lesson 24 is 'Adding Autoscaling' -- it adds the autoscaling policy, health check, and caching decision on top of the already-deployed service.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly listed as part of this capstone's success criteria?
options: The image must be pushed under the tag 'latest' only
Autoscaling must use default settings with no customization
An autoscaling policy with an explicit min AND max, each with a stated reason
The service must run without any health check endpoint
questions.explain: The success criteria explicitly call for min and max instance counts, each with a stated reason -- not defaults left untouched.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the real bar for 'done' on this capstone, beyond the service simply working?
options: Deploying to as many cloud providers as possible
Being able to explain every configuration choice you made, and why
Using the largest available GPU instance type
Finishing the capstone in under one hour
questions.explain: The lesson states directly: 'it works' isn't the bar -- being able to explain every configuration choice is what actually transfers to a real job.
